official.title: Doctoral Researcher in Real Estate Economics
official.description_text:
Aalto University is where science and art meet technology and business. We shape a sustainable future by making research breakthroughs in and across our disciplines, sparking the game changers of tomorrow and creating novel solutions to major global challenges. Our community is made up of 13 000 students, 400 professors and close to 4 500 other faculty and staff working on our dynamic campus in Espoo, Greater Helsinki, Finland. Diversity is part of who we are, and we actively work to ensure our community’s diversity and inclusiveness. This is why we warmly encourage qualified candidates from all backgrounds to join our community.
The School of Engineering drives science and innovation in industrial and built environment technologies. We are committed to educating a new generation of experts who combine technical excellence with a deep understanding of sustainable development in shaping societies. Our research focuses on sustainable built environment, mechanics and materials, multidisciplinary energy technology, and design and implementation of technical systems. The strength of our school lies in close collaboration with stakeholders across research and education. About 45 doctoral candidates and 350 master’s students graduate from the school every year. The school is home to 700 staff members, including 70 professors. To learn more, please visit eng.aalto.fi.
Real Estate Research Group at Aalto University School of Engineering, Department of Built Environment invites applications for
Doctoral Researcher in Real Estate Economics
We are seeking an excellent doctoral researcher to join the Real Estate Research Group. The position is rooted in strategic asset management and sustainable transition, primary from the perspective of real estate owner, investor and service provider.
In this position, the doctoral researcher will develop profitable transition pathways to extend the technical, functional, and financial lifespans of residential buildings and portfolios. The work includes analysing building-level technical transition costs and developing new business, financing, and implementation models, such as servitisation, crowdfunding, assets digitalization and other instruments.
The doctoral researcher will work on a project called UP-STOCK (Formulating Just Transition Paths for the Housing Stock). UP-STOCK is a co-research initiative financed by Kone Oyj, Avain Yhtiöt Oy, Helsingin kaupungin asunnot Oy, Haahtela Oy, OP Kiinteistösijoitus Oy, kaukora Oy, Business Finland, and Aalto university.
The project offers collaboration opportunities with key industry stakeholders, and the research community with our international partner universities.
The Real Estate Research Group
has around twenty researchers (doctoral researchers and postdocs) from all fields of Real Estate, including Economic Law, Land Management, Sustainable Real Estate Business, Real Estate Economics and Valuation, and Real Estate Management.
Your role and goals
Conduct doctoral research in strategic asset management and sustainable transition; publishing and communicating findings (e.g., reports, articles, conference presentations); and completing 30 ECTS of doctoral coursework
Close collaboration and co-development with the UP-STOCK project partners and stakeholders
Teaching and/or assisting in Real Estate courses (10% of work time)
Participating in applying research funding
Your experience and ambitions
Master’s degree in a relevant field such as real estate economics, construction economics, business administration and management, building technology, quantity surveying or property management with excellent study success.
Excellent collaboration skills for working with company and university partners; willingness to visit and work on the campus of the university partner as needed.
Excellent writing and presentation skills in English. Skills in Finnish are seen as an asset.
What we offer
2-year fixed-term contract with the possibility of an extension following a successful midterm review:
https://www.aalto.fi/en/programmes/aalto-doctoral-programme-in-engineering/midterm-review-of-doctoral-studies-eng
The starting salary for a doctoral researcher is €3,143/month, with the salary increasing as the research and studies progress.
The annual working time is 1612 hours. We hope that the person selected to the position will be able to start as soon as possible, and no later than 1 January 2027.
Join us!
The applications for the doctoral candidate position are to be submitted through our recruitment site (link 'Apply now’) latest by
30 October 2026 at 23.59 (EET).
Email applications will not be considered.
Please note: Aalto University’s employees should apply for the position via our internal HR system Workday (Internal Jobs) by using their existing Workday user account (not via the external webpage for open positions). If you are a student or visitor at Aalto University, please apply with your personal email address (not aalto.fi) via
Aalto University open positions
Required application documents (in a single pdf-file):
One-page motivation letter explaining why you wish to pursue doctoral research and how your background prepares you for this position
CV
Transcript of the study records
Recommendation letters if possible
Aalto University reserves the right for justified reasons to leave the position open, to extend the application period, and to consider candidates who have not submitted applications during the application period.

ai.summary: Doctoral position in real estate economics within Aalto's School of Engineering, focused on strategic asset management and sustainable transition of residential building portfolios. Work involves developing business models, financing instruments, and technical transition pathways in collaboration with industry partners.

thematic_fit.rationale: No thematic overlap. Position is grounded in real estate economics, business models, and financial instruments. Researcher's domain is human-centred XR, collaborative immersive systems, and spatial learning. The word 'sustainable' appears in both but refers to entirely different contexts (building lifecycle vs. sustainable futures broadly). No connection to immersive systems, human-computer interaction, or learning outcomes.

methodological_fit.rationale: Minimal methodological alignment. Position requires expertise in asset management, financial modeling, and economics. Researcher has strength in user studies, experimental design, and qualitative methods for evaluating human experience. No overlap in core technical or analytical approaches needed.

growth_value.rationale: Does not address researcher's identified capability gaps. Researcher needs growth in statistics, mixed-effects modelling, physiological sensing, and eye-tracking within HCI contexts. Real estate economics adds no value to this trajectory and would represent a sharp pivot away from research identity and target roles.

strategic_value.rationale: Aalto is a priority-1 institution in the researcher's target geography (Finland). However, position is in the wrong school and discipline entirely. School of Engineering Department of Built Environment does not support HCI or XR research. Supervisor network and funding are unrelated to researcher's target identity. Career path would diverge from doctoral-researcher and phd-candidate roles in immersive systems.

eligibility_flags: Position requires MSc in 'real estate economics, construction economics, business administration and management, building technology, quantity surveying or property management.' Researcher's MSc by Research in Creative Multimedia does not appear to meet stated discipline requirements.
No mention of XR, HCI, or immersive technologies in position description; no natural pathway for researcher to integrate existing expertise.
risks: Severe disciplinary mismatch would require researcher to abandon core expertise and research identity mid-trajectory.
No supervisor or group expertise in HCI, XR, or human-centred methods; mentoring would not support stated target identity.
Collaboration with industry partners (real estate, finance, construction) does not align with immersive learning or spatial cognition research networks.

eligibility_reasons: funding/salary not confirmed on the posting
